claims.text: Laser surface alloying can incorporate a controlled subsurface dispersion of WS2 nanoparticles into equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi HEA.
The incorporated WS2 forms a continuous, in situ WS2-rich tribolayer at the sliding interface.
A subsurface reservoir of dispersed WS2 particles sustains the tribolayer during sliding.
Thermal and mechanical stresses during sliding promote segregation of WS2 platelets to the contact interface.
Thermal and mechanical stresses during sliding promote alignment and activation of WS2 platelets.
The layered structure of WS2 platelets reduces shear resistance at the sliding interface.
Reduced interfacial shear resistance lowers the coefficient of friction.
The WS2-rich lubricating layer lowers the wear rate.
Laser processing produces a uniform WS2 dispersion beneath the alloy surface.
The subsurface WS2 dispersion enables self-replenishment of the lubricious layer at elevated temperatures.
Relative to untreated CrMnFeCoNi HEA, the treatment will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 30–50%.
Relative to untreated CrMnFeCoNi HEA, the treatment will produce a similar-magnitude reduction in wear rate.
The friction and wear improvements will persist from room temperature to approximately 600 °C in both inert and oxidizing atmospheres.
Prolonged high-temperature oxidizing exposure may compromise WS2 stability and degrade lubricating performance.
